slides.topic: Whole-body Substrate Metabolism — Fuel Balance & Homeostasis — source 1
slides.text:
Energy Metabolism in the Human Body 
Refers to the sum of all biochemical processes involved in the breakdown, utilization, and synthesis of energy-providing substrates throughout the entire body. These substrates primarily include carbohydrates, fats and proteins.
The process encompasses:
Catabolism: The breakdown of complex molecules into simpler forms, releasing energy.
Anabolism: The building up of compounds, which requires energy.
Energy production: The conversion of nutrients into usable cellular energy, primarily in the form of ATP.
Substrate interconversion: The transformation of one type of substrate into another, such as gluconeogenesis (eg protein to glucose) or lipogenesis (eg carbohydrate to fat).

slides.topic: Whole-body Substrate Metabolism — Fuel Balance & Homeostasis — source 4
slides.text:
Whole-body substrate metabolism 
Refers to the way the entire body takes up, utilises, stores, and switches between different energy sources (substrates) to meet its metabolic demands.
Storage and mobilization and partitioning:  The storage of excess nutrients and their mobilization when needed.
What are the metabolic consequences of dysregulated nutrient handling.
The main substrates : Carbohydrates (primarily glucose and glycogen) Lipids (fats) (fatty acids and triglycerides) Proteins (amino acids) and Ketone bodies (during fasting or carbohydrate restriction)
“Normal metabolism focuses on what is happening inside a single cell, whereas whole-body substrate metabolism focuses on where the fuel for the entire body is coming from and where it is going and how this happens.”

slides.topic: Whole-body Substrate Metabolism — Fuel Balance & Homeostasis — source 5
slides.text:
Whole-body substrate metabolism in health
Regulated by various factors, including hormones, nutritional status, and overall health.

Plays a crucial role in maintaining energy homeostasis, supporting physical activity, and adapting to different physiological and pathological states.

slides.topic: Whole-body Substrate Metabolism — Fuel Balance & Homeostasis — source 6
slides.text:
A challenge to homeostasis:  The Prandial Cycle  
The body shifts back and forth physiologically between the absorptive and the postabsorptive state.

Absorptive state:
- Absorption of energy.
- Lasts for approximately 4 hours after eating.

Postabsorptive state:
- At least 4 hours after the meal.

Fasting state: >24 hours with no food
      
Other States

slides.topic: Whole-body Substrate Metabolism — Fuel Balance & Homeostasis — source 9
slides.text:
Need to maintain energy balance and metabolic homeostasis
The most common chronic challenge to metabolic homeostasis is a prolonged mismatch between energy intake and energy expenditure, resulting in obesity and insulin resistance.

Obesity can be viewed as a state in which these regulatory systems are chronically challenged

Sustained positive energy balance cause alterations in whole-body substrate utilisation

Note: Aging - progressive loss of muscle mass, reduced mitochondrial function, and decreased insulin sensitivity.
